1.why: Four distinct relations (substitution, cause, qualification, similarity); with the text hidden none can be argued illegal.

2.why: 'In turn' and 'Thus' both mark consequence, so neither can be the unique key - if one fit the other would too; choosing between the remaining contrast/similarity pair is a coin flip.

3.why: Illustration, contrast, simultaneity and restatement are mutually exclusive relations; no option is eliminable without the text.

4.why: Concession, restatement, simultaneity and substitution are distinct enough that all four remain arguable with the source hidden.

5.why: Restatement, simultaneity, similarity and contrast are four different relations; nothing in the option set rules one out.

6.why: Same four-way spread of distinct relations; no internal contradiction or duplication to exploit.

7.why: The stem asks to emphasize a contrast between the two studies' FINDINGS: A asserts a similarity (both peer-reviewed) and reports no findings; B reports only Study A, so it contrasts nothing; C contrasts sample size, not findings; only D sets one finding against the other.

8.why: Result, comparison, concession and prior-time are distinct; all remain legal without the text.

9.why: The stem asks why the innovation MATTERS to a general reader: A and C describe only the pre-existing problem and the motivation, B describes what the innovation is without stating its significance, and only D names a consequence for people.

10.why: 'Thus' and 'For this reason' are the same causal relation, so neither can be uniquely correct; the pick between restatement and contrast is unsupported.

11.why: The stem demands a single conclusion supported by ALL THREE studies; A, C and D each report one study only and so cannot be a conclusion across three, leaving B as the only generalization.

12.why: The stem asks for a CAUTIOUS generalization a skeptic would accept; A extends one call-center result to 'most job types', D claims it is established 'beyond reasonable dispute for any job', and B dismisses the other studies outright - all three are the opposite of cautious, leaving C's hedged claim.

13.why: Contrast, consequence-chain, similarity and intensification are distinct relations; nothing eliminable.

14.why: Restatement, simultaneity, consequence and concession are four different relations; all legal with the text hidden.

15.why: Illustration, similarity, contrast and result are mutually exclusive; no option self-destructs.

16.why: Sequence-closing, similarity, concession and consequence are distinct; nothing eliminable from the set alone.

17.why: 'At the same time' can read as simultaneity or concession, so it is not a clean duplicate of 'On the other hand'; all four stay legal.

18.why: Intensification, contrast, illustration and time-reference are distinct relations; none is ruled out without the text.

19.why: Sequence, concession, similarity and summary are distinct; no elimination available.

20.why: Result, intensification, similarity and concession are distinct; all four remain arguable.

21.why: Simultaneity, restatement, substitution and conditional-alternative are distinct relations; nothing eliminable.

22.why: The stem asks to emphasize a DIFFERENCE in migration distance between the two species; A asserts a likeness, and C and D each give one species' distance with nothing to compare it against, so only B states both figures in contrast.

23.why: The stem asks for a disconnect between felt alertness and actual performance; D gives only study design, C only the 8-hour group, and A gives performance with no self-rating, so only B pairs the self-rating with the contrary result.

24.why: Simultaneity, concession, consequence and summary are distinct relations; no option eliminable from the set alone.
